voice_spoof_detector.note: pretrained inference, no training -- evidence-gate run per Principle 11. Threshold calibrated via best_f1_threshold on bonafide + train-split spoof only (round 2), then applied unchanged to held_out -- round 1 used an uncalibrated 0.5 default.

document_consistency_detector.note: pretrained OCR-VL + our own QR cross-check logic, no training -- evidence-gate run per Principle 11. Run on Google Colab (T4 GPU), not locally -- paddlepaddle-gpu proved unstable across four distinct low-level Windows driver/library errors in a row (DLL collision, cudnn version mismatch, opencv package collision, cudnn execution failure); see docs/FUTURE_INTEGRATIONS.md item 2. Detector and metrics code run unmodified from the repo. Threshold calibrated via best_f1_threshold on bonafide + train-split fraud only (round 2), then applied unchanged to held_out -- round 1 used an uncalibrated 0.5 default, which is why round 1 showed recall=0.7125 vs round 2's 0.9125 at the same false_positive_rate (0.25 both rounds -- the same 10/40 bonafide docs were misflagged either way; the quantized field-mismatch score never put a bonafide doc exactly between 0.25 and 0.5).

fusion_adversarial_eval.note: Section 6 evidence gate -- weighted XGBoost+LightGBM+Autoencoder fusion, same held-out set as the individual *_adversarial_eval entries, for direct comparison.

reasons: The autoencoder's low recall (0.43) on off-hours mid-amount transactions indicates it relies on strong distribution drift to generate high reconstruction error.

Masking the transaction within standard business hours and lowering the amount reduces its baseline anomaly score, directly targeting the autoencoder's tendency to treat low-value daytime events as benign.
autoencoder_weakness_round2_transaction_.note: Section 8 step 6 -- targeted second round on the weakest signal found in step 5.
